newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. envoy arrives in Cyprus for talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy arrives in Cyprus for talks.

text.p: A United Nations mediator arrived in divided Cyprus on Wednesday for a new round of talks with rival sides in an attempt to end the stalemate in the decades old dispute.
U.N. special representative for Cyprus Han Sung-joo of South Korea will discuss preparations for face-to-face talks with the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.
"We think that there is a window of opportunity this year, hopefully during the first half of this year," Han told reporters on arrival.

"I will try to find areas of agreement between the two communities, between the leaders and report to the Secretary General as how to proceed from there. Hopefully we could force drive the situation where the Secretary-General can invite the leaders to discuss the matter face to face, and in direct talks," he added.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops landed in the north of the island in response to a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece.
U.N. attempts to reunite Cyprus under a federal system have failed.

Tensions between the two sides have risen in recent weeks after the Cyprus government announced plans to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia, and Turkey said it would take whatever action was needed to ensure they were not deployed.
Han said the tension made possibilities of a meeting more difficult, but not impossible.

An application by Cyprus to join the European Union served as a new incentive for a solution to the problem even before the latest crisis, since negotiations with the EU would be more complicated if the island remained partitioned.
Turkish Cypriots proclaimed their own state in 1983 in the north of the island, where more than 30,000 Turkish troops are stationed. It is recognised only by Ankara.

Han is due to have at least three separate meetings with President Glafcos Clerides, who heads the internationally-recognised Greek Cypriot-led government, and Rauf Denktash, the Turkish Cypriot leader who presides over the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus. He will host a lunch for representatives of Greek and Turkish Cypriot political parties.

"I would like to get into the substance of the issues which have been the concern of both communities as well as of the international community.... we do not have a counter proposal as such, but certainly we have ideas and hope we have enough basis to have discussions," Han said.
